title: Gib and cotter joint
parts_note: a round rod with a square end, a strap that wraps it, and the cotter split into a tapered cotter plus one or two hooked gibs
verified_against: Unwin, Elements of Machine Design, 1899, page 179 figures 130 and 131 (gib and cotter proportions, unit = the breadth b) and page 178 figure 127 (simple cottered joint). Out of copyright, from archive.org, kept in reference/. The strength checks are the socket-and-spigot check set from NPTEL IIT Kharagpur module 4 lesson 2, carried across to a square section: see check_source below.
check_source: Every check is the matching socket-and-spigot cotter check with the circular area replaced by the square one: pi/4 d^2 becomes B^2, (d2 - d1) becomes (Bo - B). The cotter joint those formulas came from is verified against NPTEL module 4 lesson 2 and tested in tests/test_book_problems.py. Nothing here is an invented ratio: anything Unwin does not give is sized by a check, not by a proportion.
why_a_gib: A plain cotter pushes the two sides of the strap apart as it is driven. The gib is the other half of the same slot, with hooked ends that wrap the strap and hold it together, so the taper can be steeper. Unwin page 179.

default_stresses_mpa.source: same working values as the other cotter joints in this tool

breadth_split.source: Unwin 1899 page 179, figures 130 and 131. One gib: 5/8 cotter + 3/8 gib. Two gibs: 5/16 + 3/8 + 5/16. The unit is the total breadth b.

t.meaning: thickness of the gib and cotter
t.source: Unwin 1899 page 179, figures 130 and 131: thickness 0.25 x the breadth b

taper.range: 1 in 24 to 1 in 48 for a plain cotter; 1 in 8 to 1 in 16 when a screw stops it slacking back

sized_by_check.B: rod end square side: raised until the rod end passes tension across the slot and crushing
sized_by_check.Bo: strap outer square side: raised until the strap passes tension across the slot and crushing
sized_by_check.b: total breadth of gib and cotter: from double shear, P = 2 b t tau
sized_by_check.a: rod end beyond the slot: from shear of the rod end, P = 2 a B tau
sized_by_check.c: strap beyond the slot: from shear of the strap end, P = 2 c (Bo - B) tau

gib_hook.note: how far the hooked end of the gib laps over the strap, times the cotter thickness

hook_height.note: height of the hooked lip, times the cotter thickness

cotter_overhang.note: how far the cotter stands proud, times the rod diameter

rod_length.note: length of round rod shown each side, times the rod diameter

corner_radius.note: radius on the outside corners of the strap

end_wall.note: strap metal closing over the rod tip, times the rod end side; a modelling choice, not a check

indian_standards_to_check: IS 2016 / IS 1367 for any fastener used with it (verify)
units: SI: mm, N, MPa. First angle projection (Indian practice, SP 46).
